chapter: Later career, civil service and jazz seminars
title: Civil service job at City College
summary: He passed civil service exams and worked at City College from November 1957, first in the mail room, improving a stencil card process.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: Well, when did you get into this education thing you're talking about?

Well, I got to taking the civil service exam, passed it, went to the Park Department. I was taking another exam. Of course, we're always taking exams. And I passed that. And so I switched from there and went on up to the Board of Higher Education, and they sent me over to City College, been there ever since.
That was 19- -- I believe that's November, 1957.
And what did you do? What do you do?

Well, first it was in the mail room. Then (being) (unintelligible) worked in the post office (before) (unintelligible) it was easy for me, but then this (unintelligible) we'll show you how to operate these machines. So I learned it fast,

and I instituted something over there that wasn't done before. (crossed out: Asked the) secretary (crossed out: to) attached a certain (crossed out: they were) way for cards to be typing them wrong, and I instituted how to type them the right way so the crosswise was lengthwise, because it would come through quicker, and you save a lot of time and money because the carbon double up and tap the stencil. I said, no good.
Well, they say, well, I've always been doing it this way. Well, I say, that's the wrong way.

You do it this way. So they (unintelligible), said, well, how (unintelligible). I say, there's a diagram in the stencil. It's a square. That's where you use it from that, postal card, any size card. Don't put them crosswise because you'd (unintelligible) the stencil for running off on the mimeograph paper is across -- left to right or right to left. But this is down.
